design.ciMethod: 95 % confidence interval of Sen's slope from the Mann-Kendall variance (Gilbert 1987)
design.text: Hansen loss has one trend, over 2011-2025 (the years Hansen processed with one consistent method), never across the 2011 method change; 2001-2010 are shown but not tested. Mann-Kendall test on yearly values with Sen's slope, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the tested cells of each variable. Rules fixed before seeing the results (autocorrelation, satellite drift) applied as written. The shuffled-years check shuffles the years of every cell and reruns the whole procedure; shuffling each square on its own checks against memoryless noise that is independent between squares. The simulated-trend check adds to the shuffled series a linear trend equal to the median |Sen slope| of the real significant cells; the same test trend is added to every square, and the detection rate is an average over squares with very different noise.

acrossBreak.note: Not used: one test across the 2011 method change gives a rising Amazon trend while the official PRODES series falls.

hansenConsistency.text: Hansen loss in the Brazilian Amazon tracks the official INPE PRODES series in 2001-2010 (r = 0.85, Hansen/PRODES ratio 1.15) but not in 2011-2025 (r = 0.2, ratio 2.7), after Hansen reprocessed its data from 2011. Testing 2001-2025 in one piece gives an increasing trend for the Amazon (p = 0.047125) while PRODES shows a decreasing trend (p = 0.014196): a result of the 2011 method change. So the published loss trend uses only 2011-2025, the years Hansen processed with one consistent method; all loss years 2001-2025 are shown, and 2001-2010 are real Hansen data from the earlier method that are not tested for a trend. In 2011-2025 the whole-Amazon Hansen series shows an increasing trend (p = 0.0075332) and PRODES shows an increasing trend (p = 0.047761); for comparison, 2001-2010 gives no clear trend for Hansen (p = 0.1074) and a decreasing trend for PRODES (p = 0.012266). Where Hansen sees more loss, MODIS tree cover falls more (r = -0.79 in 2001-2010, -0.47 in 2011-2025).

d1Drift.rule: If |r| >= 0.5 for a variable, its test ends in 2020 (like land surface temperature); otherwise it keeps 2001-2025 and 2021-2025 are flagged as satellite drift years.
